solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ferret out to catch a plague

indicators.note: to catch means the first piece closes round the second, holding it inside

parts.note: to ferret out something is to hunt it down

explanation.surface: A ferret is sent down a burrow to catch whatever pest is plaguing the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to catch' puts A inside HUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: To plague someone is to trouble them persistently, as a ghost or a worry does when it haunts.

clue.text: Panic over salt in sweet cake

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the next one

parts.note: a flap is a state of panic, as in 'getting in a flap'
an old salt is a sailor, and Jack (Jack Tar) is another name for a sailor

explanation.surface: Someone panics after spilling salt into the mixture for a sweet cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt' looks like a cooking ingredient, but it means a sailor, as does JACK.
explanation.definitionFit: A flapjack is a chewy oat bar baked with butter and syrup, sold in Britain as a sweet cake.

clue.text: Brouhaha rare for beloved

parts.note: a brouhaha is a fuss, which is ado
rare meat is still red in the middle

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a fuss over something rare has replaced love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rare' means red, as in an underdone steak, not scarce.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone beloved is dearly loved, worshipped even: a synonym in the past-participle form.

clue.text: Idiot preserved meat

definitions.meaning: ..., or jerky, is meat cured by drying in strips

explanation.surface: An insult hurled at someone, followed by a deli label.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerk is slang for a fool, and also a dried, cured meat, now usually called jerky.

clue.text: Daffy bird

definitions.meaning: a bird that lays eggs in other birds' nests

explanation.surface: Daffy Duck, the cartoon bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuckoo is slang for crazy, and is also the name of the familiar bird with a two-note call.

clue.text: Odd bits removed, see ship in bottle that's silvery-white

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a magnum is a large wine bottle, twice the standard size

indicators.note: dropping the odd-numbered letters of these words leaves only the even ones

explanation.surface: Someone with odd bits removed admires a model ship in a bottle that gleams silvery-white.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd bits removed' works across both words 'see ship' together, keeping the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnesium is a light metal whose fresh surface is a shiny silvery-white colour.

clue.text: Possibly bitter about everything, commercial singer

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the others

parts.note: bitter is one kind of beer, hence 'possibly'
everything is all
a commercial is an ad

explanation.surface: A jingle singer turned bitter about the whole business of commercials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitter' looks like a mood; it is the British pale ale, so 'Possibly' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A balladeer is someone who sings ballads, a singer of story songs.

clue.text: Name top city in Western Asia

parts.note: to dub someone is to name them
A1 means first-rate or top, written as AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A quiz question: name the leading city in Western Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubai is the largest city of the United Arab Emirates, on the Persian Gulf in Western Asia.

clue.text: Reportedly, logo for plate clashed?

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard spoken, so the word is swapped for one that sounds the same

parts.note: a logo is a symbol

explanation.surface: Rumour has it a company logo was printed on a plate that clashed with the décor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plate clashed' is a whimsical description: a cymbal is a metal plate struck against another.
explanation.definitionFit: A cymbal is a brass disc, a plate in effect, that drummers clash together.

clue.text: Lead from pistol puncturing kidneys from behind, assassin hiding

indicators.note: puncturing means the first piece goes into the second
read from behind means the word is reversed

parts.note: reins is an old word for the kidneys

indicators.note: the lead from a word is its leading, first letter

explanation.surface: A bullet from a hidden assassin's pistol pierces the victim's kidneys from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' is not the metal of a bullet but the first letter P. 'from behind' turns REINS into SNIER; 'puncturing' puts P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniper is a gunman who shoots from a concealed position, an assassin in hiding.

clue.text: Man trapping a rabbit for sport

indicators.note: trapping means the first piece holds the others inside it

parts.note: a man in chess is a piece, such as the king
to rabbit, in British slang, is to chatter, as is to yak

explanation.surface: A hunter traps a rabbit for sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbit' is British slang for talk on and on, here YAK, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Kayaking, paddling a small canoe-like boat, is a water sport.

clue.text: Indian scholar not to mention in hell

indicators.note: in means one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: the pit is hell
not to mention means in addition, which is and

explanation.surface: An Indian scholar finds himself in hell, not to mention other troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: A pandit is a learned Hindu teacher, the origin of the English word pundit.

clue.text: Time off for some member

parts.note: meat that has gone off is said to be high

explanation.surface: A club member gets time off for some reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' means a limb, not a club member.
explanation.definitionFit: A member is a limb of the body, and the thigh is the upper part of the leg.

clue.text: Disease in cattle fed string — feed on grass

indicators.note: fed means a piece is put inside the other, like food into a mouth

parts.note: BSE is bovine spongiform encephalopathy, 'mad cow disease'
a string of things is a row

explanation.surface: Diseased cattle are fed string instead of being left to feed on grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed' is the insertion signal, not part of the definition, which is only 'feed on grass'.
explanation.definitionFit: To browse is for animals to graze, feeding on grass, leaves or shoots.

clue.text: Turn hand and flip one's lid

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game
a hand is a bunch of bananas

explanation.surface: A card player takes a turn, sees the hand and loses their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hand' is not cards but a bunch of bananas, as fruit sellers call it.
explanation.definitionFit: To go bananas is slang for getting wildly angry or excited, the same idiom as flipping one's lid.

clue.text: Do business right

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business
OK means right, correct

explanation.surface: A slogan urging people to conduct business correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like an auxiliary verb; it is the definition, to prepare food or to fiddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To do a meal is to prepare it; to cook can also mean to falsify, as in cooking the books.

clue.text: Photograph, all the same

definitions.meaning: a single photograph, especially one from a film

explanation.surface: Two ideas set side by side: a picture, and a shrug of 'even so'.
explanation.definitionFit: A still is a frozen frame or posed photo; still also means nonetheless.

clue.text: Main tune hasn't complex melody at the end

indicators.note: complex means the letters are tangled into a new arrangement
at the end picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A critic says a tune isn't complex, though the melody picks up at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' rearranges HASNT into SHANT; 'at the end' takes Y from melody. 'Main' is the sea, not the chief.
explanation.definitionFit: A shanty is a sailor's work song, a tune of the sea, which crosswords call the main.

clue.text: Slimy thing, sock

definitions.meaning: to sock someone is to punch them

explanation.surface: Something slimy found in a sock.
explanation.definitionFit: A slug is a slimy garden creature; to slug is to hit hard, as is to sock.

clue.text: Confront someone winning by four, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: to face them ready to fight
four is a square number, so a player four up is jokingly ...

explanation.surface: Facing up to a rival who leads by four.
explanation.definitionFit: Squaring up means taking a fighting stance against someone; four, being two squared, makes a lead of four whimsically square.

clue.text: First step, not last, to reach a country

indicators.note: not last means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a gambit is an opening move, a first step

explanation.surface: Advice on the first step needed to reach a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not last' cuts T from GAMBIT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gambia is a small West African country along the Gambia River.

clue.text: Gentle spirit coming over in mountain

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ben is Scottish for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming over means the word turns upside down, read backwards

parts.note: gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A gentle ghost drifts over in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' looks like a ghost; it is the drink. 'coming over' turns it upside down in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Benign means kindly and mild, a synonym for gentle.

clue.text: Huge figure enough to completely stuff bowler?

definitions.meaning: a bowler is a hat, so enough to fill it is a ...

explanation.surface: A huge amount that would stuff a cricket bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' looks like the cricketer; it is the round hard hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatful is as much as a hat holds, and colloquially a large quantity, such as goals scored.

clue.text: Warm to a beastly home

parts.note: a sty is a home for pigs, a beast's home

explanation.surface: A welcome made warm to an animal's home.
explanation.definitionFit: Toasty is an informal word for comfortably warm.

clue.text: Extract from screenwriter, seriously short

indicators.note: Extract from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A film writer, seriously pushed, produces only a short extract.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse means brief and abrupt, using few words, so short in speech.

clue.text: Alluring trap in spelling?

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: casting a spell is magic
a net is a trap

explanation.surface: A spelling test set as an alluring trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spelling' is casting spells, not writing words.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnetic person or personality attracts others, which is what alluring means.

clue.text: First of all, can everyone read this? Sure thing

indicators.note: First of all means the first letter of all the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A teacher asks whether everyone can read this, and the answer is: of course.
explanation.definitionFit: Cert is British slang, short for certainty, for something sure to happen, such as a racing favourite.

clue.text: Grey clothes on — yes!

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here: the first piece dresses, so wraps, the second

parts.note: grey hair means old, so aged
re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone delighted to put on grey clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is a verb, not garments: the grey word dresses the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'agreed!' is an emphatic way of saying yes, giving consent.

clue.text: Load ton on mythological ship

parts.note: a ton is a hundred, C in Roman numerals
the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A ton of goods loaded on Jason's legendary ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ton' is not a weight but a hundred, C in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is the goods carried by a ship, its load.

clue.text: Split open on the outside, tine originally prodding uncooked sausage

indicators.note: on the outside means the first piece wraps the rest

parts.note: to burst is to split open

indicators.note: prodding means the letter is pushed into the word

parts.note: uncooked means raw

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fork's tine prods an uncooked sausage, whose skin splits open.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertions nest: the tine's letter prods into the raw word first, then the split word wraps the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A bratwurst is a German sausage, usually of pork, grilled or fried.
